title: Cognitive light cones have expanded over evolutionary time

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cognitive light cones have expanded over evolutionary time

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The volume of possible cognitive light cones (spatio-temporal boundaries of agents' goals) has presumably kept expanding over evolutionary time, through innovations in body structure that drastically enlarge the cognitive boundary, although some lineages contract it permanently or in particular life stages.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Presumably, the volume of possible cognitive light cones keeps expanding with evolutionary time (although some lineages can contract it, permanently or during specific ontogenetic life stages). Over evolutionary scales, there have been “inflationary leaps” – innovations in body structure which drastically increase the cognitive boundary of viable selves.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective”. Scope: Evolution of agents across the tree of life

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A comparative proxy analysis is conceivable and phylogenies are public. However, the core multivariate trait is not standardized, taxonomic coverage would be highly biased, and broad historical expansion cannot be cleanly resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define cognitive-light-cone volume from measurable sensing horizons, memory duration, and action reach across extant taxa, reconstruct ancestral values, and test for a temporal trend with lineage-specific contractions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ancestral reconstruction is sensitive to survivorship and trait definitions.

Comparable cognition-range traits are not assembled across life.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.2

discriminating power: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.3

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The historical claim is that possible cognitive boundaries have expanded, with admitted contractions. Paleontological datasets can track bodies and sensory organs. They cannot track the volume of goals an extinct agent could pursue. Because the claim already allows contractions, almost any disparity curve is compatible with it. The trend is not a distinct empirical statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Body-plan disparity through time can be counted from fossils and phylogenies. A cognitive light cone is the author's goal-boundary, and expansions of morphology do not measure expansions of that boundary.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The light cone is defined in cognitive terms that fossils do not record.

Morphological complexity is a different variable, and lineages that simplify anatomy are allowed by the claim.
